text:
Maya: Quick sync — finished first pass quant experiments for newmodel-x (14B). Posting numbers and a short rollout suggestion. Link to full bench: https://redwood.internal/bench/newmodel-x :eyes:

Sam: Nice. Can you paste the perf/cost deltas here?

Maya: Sure, paste below (microbench on rtx-a40 pool, batch=1 latency median):
```
newmodel-x (14B) fp16: 7.9 ms/token, 0.0034 $/k-token -> baseline
newmodel-x (14B) int8: 9.6 ms/token, 0.0018 $/k-token, avg quality delta vs fp16: -0.8% absolute (eval set A)
newmodel-x (14B) int8+remap: 9.1 ms/token, 0.0019 $/k-token, quality delta -0.5%
opt-13b (int8): 10.2 ms/token, 0.0016 $/k-token, quality delta -1.3%
```

Maya: Note: int8 increases latency slightly due to dequant overhead but halves token cost. Eval breakdown: chat-turn PU and long-form summarization skew quality loss higher on prompts with code.

Liam: What's our product risk tolerance? Eva, any guardrails from GTN on quality/regression?

Eva: For GTN we can accept up to ~1% quality drop on average for non-critical flows. Anything above 0.5% needs a canary and prompt-level gating. Code-heavy flows are higher sensitivity.

Sam: Suggestion: staged rollout config — route 25% of requests to int8 for 48h with canary tests against eval set. If pass, expand to 60% while keeping heavy-code tag pinned to fp16.

Rod: Ops note — int8 model variant consumes ~0.8x GPU memory vs fp16 on same container, so we can pack more replicas. That helps throughput and overall unit cost beyond token pricing.

Maya: Proposed rollout snippet (quick):
```
{ "model": "newmodel-x", "variants": ["fp16","int8"], "routing": { "default": {"int8": 0.6, "fp16": 0.4}, "tags": {"code-heavy": {"fp16": 1.0}} }, "canary": {"int8": 0.25, "duration_hours": 48, "checks": ["eval-A-delta<0.8%","latency_95<int:120ms"]} }
```

Liam: Two quick asks: 1) add per-prompt fingerprinting so we can retro-fit which prompts regressed; 2) include a fallback policy when quality delta exceeds threshold (auto-route to fp16).

Maya: Agreed on both. I wired a simple prompt-hash header in the test harness already. Can wire auto-fallback via policy: `quality_monitor -> route(fp16)` trigger.

Sam: Who will own the canary monitoring? Eng-oncall or ML infra?

Rod: ML infra will own instrumentation, eng-oncall will get paged on SLA/latency regressions. I'll add dashboards: tokens/cost by variant, eval-delta over time, prompt-fingerprint distribution.

ci-deploy-bot: ci:build #467 passed for newmodel-x:int8 — artifact: gcr.io/redwood/newmodel-x:int8@sha256:abcd1234

Eva: For GTN comms — I'll draft a short note: expected unit cost reduction ~45% for standard chat, recommended rollout plan and product impact matrix. Will share for review. :thumbsup:

Maya: Plan: start canary tomorrow 09:00 PT, run 48h, report results in this thread. If we see >0.8% avg delta or >2% spike in critical prompt set, rollback.

Sam: Sounds good. If canary passes, let's do 2-step expansion (60% -> 90%) over next week with continued monitoring.

Maya: Thanks — will push canary config and invite folks to the dashboard.

Liam: great work, thanks team.
